subject.title: feat(ios): Siri App Intent integration — native "Hey Siri, ask OpenClaw..." support

question: Should OpenClaw add first-party iOS Siri/AppIntent execution, and should it route through Talk Mode, paired `node.event`/operator chat, or a hardened `/hooks/agent` boundary?
rationale: The codebase already has adjacent chat, Talk, share-extension, and hook primitives, but choosing one affects auth, session state, confirmation, background execution, and spoken-output policy.

options.title: Design-gated native intent
options.body: Approve native Siri/AppIntent support only after maintainers choose the auth boundary, session semantics, confirmation policy, and spoken-reply behavior; then require real iOS proof.

options.title: Limit to Talk Mode launch
options.body: Scope the first-party intent to launching or foregrounding Talk Mode, leaving parameterized background Siri questions out of scope for now.

options.title: Keep webhook workaround external
options.body: Decline first-party Siri agent execution until demand or extension APIs justify the security surface, leaving Shortcuts plus webhook as the workaround.

recommendation.title: Design-gated native intent
recommendation.body: Approve native Siri/AppIntent support only after maintainers choose the auth boundary, session semantics, confirmation policy, and spoken-reply behavior; then require real iOS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent iOS Talk and product-surface history makes this the best available owner for the product-boundary choice.
